newsitem.title: CHINA: China's zinc exports seen at 180,000 T in 1996.
newsitem.headline: China's zinc exports seen at 180,000 T in 1996.

text.p: Low international prices will help restrict Chinese exports of zinc to around 180,000 tonnes in 1996, a China National Nonferrous Metals Industry Corp (CNNC) analyst said on Tuesday.
China exported 191,535 tonnes of unwrought zinc and zinc alloys in 1995, down 31.1 percent from the year before, official figures show.
Zinc imports to China were likely to total less than 60,000 tonnes this year, Feng Juncong of CNNC's Techno-Economic Research Institute told Reuters.

A possible rise in world zinc prices could boost Chinese exports in the next few years, but production limits and local requirements meant exports were unlikely to top 300,000 tonnes a year, regardless of the strength of foreign demand, she said.
Chinese zinc output totalled 770,100 tonnes in the first nine months of 1996, down 5.36 percent from the same period of 1995, official figures show.
Falling profits for China's many small smelters would force some to close as demand for concentrate forced up prices, Feng said in a report to a metals conference in Beijing.
The development of China's car industry and the nation's ongoing construction boom would fuel soaring Chinese zinc consumption over the next few years, she said.
"In the not too distant future, China will rank among the world's forerunners in the consumption of...zinc," she said.
